item.title: Machine runner swarm changelog
item.description:
The release notes are on GitHub Releases. Read the notes of every release between yours and the one that you install before you upgrade: the project follows Semantic Versioning and starts at 0.x, so a minor release can contain breaking changes, which the notes list first.

A CircleCI job writes the notes of each release from the Conventional Commits on main, with the rules in cliff.toml. Nobody edits this file by hand, and the release job never commits to main. Each release bundle contains a CHANGELOG.md with the notes of every release, and you can create the same text with git cliff. Refer to Releasing for how versions and notes are made, and to Contributing for the commit types and for how to mark a breaking change.

item.title: Migrate from Docker Compose
item.description:
Warning

Machine runner swarm no longer ships the Docker Compose setup. The files docker-compose.yml, base-image/, convenience-image/, and machine-image/ were removed in the Swarm rewrite, and the change is marked [BREAKING] in the changelog. Find the old files with git log -- docker-compose.yml.

The old setup restarted the same container after each job, so jobs did not get a clean environment. The Swarm stack creates a new container for every job (Why not plain Docker Compose?). This page covers Linux hosts, which the old setup supported. Your job configs, resource classes and tokens can stay.

What changed

Old setup Swarm stack
Services base, convenience, and machine in docker-compose.yml One service for each resource class in linux/stack/runners.yaml. The continuous runner is linux/stack/persistent.yaml
restart: unless-stopped, which restarts the same container restart_policy: condition: any, which creates a new container
Token in a .env file as CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_AUTH_TOKEN, visible in docker inspect Swarm secret <SERVICE>-token, which holds a runner config file
The same CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME for every replica {{.Node.Hostname}}-<SERVICE>-{{.Task.Slot}}, unique for each replica
Dockerfiles that build the runner into an image A stock image, with the runner mounted from the volume runner-bin (Images)
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE and CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR in the service environment The same variables, in the stack file. Cleanup is "false" on Linux

Migrate

  1. Name the classes. A Swarm service must have the name of its resource class. To keep your classes and tokens, name each service after the class it replaces, for example base. For new classes, create them.

  2. Prepare the host. Docker Engine is already there. Start Swarm and install nothing else: the runner-distributor service installs the runner on every node (Start Swarm).

  3. Create the secrets. Use the token of each class, the value of CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_AUTH_TOKEN in your old .env file (Create the secrets).

  4. Choose the images. The old convenience service maps to cimg/base or another cimg image, and base to a stock image with your tools. Move extra tools from your Dockerfiles into a derived image (Linux: bring your own image).

  5. Edit the stack file. Rename or copy the services, set your old replica counts, and keep only what you need. The old machine service becomes linux/stack/persistent.yaml (Resource classes).

  6. Deploy next to the old setup. Both can run at once, because the runner names differ. Check that the new runners show up in the inventory. If a new service keeps a class whose old runners are busy, the token proxy sees running tasks at its first start, cannot tell whose they are, and refuses the present runners until their idle timeout, or until you run the command below once the old runners are idle. New classes avoid this (Restart the proxy).

    docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_<SERVICE>

  7. Stop the old setup. When the old runners are idle, run docker compose down in the old directory. A running job is stopped after the Compose grace period, so wait for a quiet period.

  8. Clean up. Delete the old .env files, which hold tokens in clear text. If you created new classes, delete the old tokens and classes in CircleCI.

Behavior to expect

  • Runner updates. The runner is an exact pin by default: the newest version that CI tests, bumped by each release. Set 3.1, 3 or current to follow CircleCI’s manifest (Upgrade the runner on Linux).
  • Sudo. The default classes keep passwordless sudo, as the old images did. The hardened class removes it (Concepts).
  • Fixed replicas. The stack does not scale by itself, and a node that dies is not replaced (Capacity and concurrency).
  • Startup time. A new container starts for every job, so a job waits about 10 seconds longer for the next claim, plus the task agent download. Add replicas for busy classes.
  • Swarm on one host. Swarm mode is required even on a single host. The helper and the install page start it on the loopback address, so nothing is exposed.
  • Working directory. The runner no longer removes the working directory on Linux, because it runs as another user than the jobs. A new container for every job leaves nothing behind, but a persistent class (the old machine service) keeps files between jobs, so start its jobs with a cleanup step (Working directory cleanup).
